page.layout: One page of running text. Marginal notes in the right margin, beside the lines "commentum Re-" and "fine excidit". Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.l: 15. 2. Cuicunque prædicatur verbum, id
assequitur, quod Deus intendit: nam
non potest vacuum ad Deum reverti Esai.55.
11.[?] Ergo si Deus per verbum reproborum
obedientiam intenderet, procul dubio obedi-
rent. Non ergo Deus sine per verbum
intento, excidere potest. Et Deus
Ezech. 2. v. 7. aperte dicit Israelitas non obeditu-
ros, vult tamen Prophetam loqui; quasi
vero Deus diceret eo loci, scio eos non obe-
diturox, volo tamen & intendo ut obediant.
Sed audiat lector mirum commentum
Re-monstrantium, qui volunt, postquam
Deus fine excidit, manere tamen hypotheticam
intentionem in Deo. O prodigium! Deus
etiam hodie habet intentionem conditiona-
lem salvandi Judam: & Pharaonis obedien-
tiam vult, intentione scilicet optativa, e-
tiam postquam æternis pænis est adjudica-
tus.
16. 3. Id Deo non competit, quod in
scripturis habetur, pro gravi judicio &
maledictione: at consilio & intento fine
excidere est reproborum maledictio Ps. 2. 4.
Psal. 33. v. 10. Esai. 8. v. 9. Esai. 29. v. 7.
Jer. 19. v. 7. Job. 15. v. 12. 13. Sic vero Deo in
cœlis ridenti irrita & vana hominum consilia,
ii in terris scommatum talionem referre
pos-sent.
4. Quod est divinæ perfectionis nota,
ejus contrarium Deo affingi non potest. At ad
finem intentum pervenire, est tale: Ergo

page.notes: Printed text in the margin: "Apolog. ǂ" (the mark is uncertain) and "17.fol.161". The reference "Esai.55" is uncertain: the numeral is printed in an old form. The final line "S &c." sits at the right below the text and is taken as the catchword. The running head is printed NVNQVAM and is given with u as NUNQUAM. The page number 173 is partly worn.
